title: Live imaging and quantitation of insect feeding-induced Ca2+ signal using GCaMP3-based system in Nicotiana benthamiana
protocol: Fill each well of sterile polystyrene 96 well-flat bottom tissue culture plates with 0.2 mL solid MS nutrients.
Cut off both cotyledons from 8-day-old GCaMP3 seedlings using a sterile scalpel blade.
Place the removed cotyledons horizontally in each well of the 96-well plate using sterile forceps.
Transfer three starved apterous adult aphids from a plastic petri dish to the surface of each cotyledon in the wells using a soft lip brush.
Cover the 96-well plate with sterile plastic wrap.
Perform all operations in an aseptic condition using ultra-clean benches.
Place the plates in the PRX-450D incubator at 24°C–26°C with a 16 h/8 h light/dark photoperiod for 24 hours.
Maintain removed cotyledons on MS medium in the incubator for at least 24 hours to eliminate calcium flow effects caused by physical damage.
After 24 hours, remove plates from the incubator and uncover plastic wrap for 1 hour to ventilate and remove water vapor.
Gently transfer starved apterous adult aphids into an empty petri dish using a soft lip brush.
Transfer three starved apterous adult aphids onto the cotyledon surface in each well (except four wells as control) using a soft lip brush.
Rapidly wrap the 96-well plate in plastic wrap to prevent aphid escape.
Open Leica Application Suite X software and set the microscope parameters as follows.
Set acquisition mode to xyt.
Select ET GFP filter for imaging.
Acquire images at 16 bit resolution.
Use image format of 1024 × 1024 pixels with 2 × 2 binning.
Set exposure time to 300 ms and gain to 2 (Gain List: low noise & high well).
Select “TL light” or “SLI light” as optical mode for bright-field illumination.
Adjust the intensity of TL light or SLI light to a minimum degree, then gradually increase it.
Place the 96-well plate with cotyledons and aphids on the microscope stage.
Adjust the zoom lens to focus on the samples in one well under bright-field illumination (zoom is about 2.0–3.0).
Ensure clear observation of the leaf in the control group.
Detect the GFP fluorescence of leaves in the control group.
GFP fluorescence represents the background fluorescence intensity of GCaMP3 leaves.
Set the parameters appropriately for the 96-well plate.
Move the 96-well plate gently to focus on samples with aphids.
Set the “Exposure time” to 300 ms.
Define the recording time, such as 5 minutes or until calcium flow vanishes.
Capture emitted fluorescence using a Leica DFC9000 GT digital camera (sCMOS).
Record fluorescence dynamics at the area of aphid bites.
Use the control group to adjust LFSM parameters for eliminating background noise.
Wait patiently for aphids to adapt to the new environment before recording.
Observe aphids' movements and antennae behavior to predict biting moments.
Open LAX software and select “Standard Configuration”.
Click “OK”.
Select “Open Project” in settings and load files with .lif suffix.
Click on “Process” – “Show Gallery” to view captured images.
Use “Annotations” to add symbols to pictures as needed.
Select the start image of the video and click on “Set Start”.
Select the last image and click on “Set End”.
Open the LAX software and load files of interest with the suffix .lif.
Click on “Process” – “Show Gallery” to view the captured images.
Select the start image of the video, click on “Set Start” in the middle menu.
In the same way, select the last image and click on “Set End”.
Right-click on the new file and select “Export” - “As MPEG-4” - “Frames/sec” to export the video.
Click the “Stack profile” button in the pulldown menu of “Tools”.
Tick the box “All in one”.
Choose the shape of the selected region.
Select the aphid biting area.
Right-click on the curves and select “Export”.
Select “Excel” to export all fluorescence values.
Export the corresponding time data of the selected region in every frame as an excel file.
Click the Rectangle or Oval icon in the upper right toolbar.
Drag the mouse button to select an area.
Observe the fluorescence value displayed in the selected region.
Note the mean intensity of fluorescence value of the selected region in every frame presented as a numerical point in the middle area of the interface.
Automatically link the points as a curve with one color.
Repeat operations to select multiple regions near Ca2+ flux occurring positions.
Right-click on the curves and select “Export” and then “Excel”.
Export all fluorescence values along with its corresponding time data of the selected region in every frame as an excel file.

Calculate the fractional fluorescence changes (ΔF/F) using ΔF/F = (F − F0)/F0, where F0 is the average baseline fluorescence from the first 5 frames before aphids feeding and “F” is the current fluorescence value.
Average the ratios of multiple regions to obtain a single ΔF/F ratio for analysis.
Collect data for analysis and make into Ca2+ flux dynamic curve mode using Prism7 software.
